The two pieces here — type-and-it-finds-it, and tapping a label to see everything under it from either spot — both match what I want, and they're solid.

But I wouldn't call the whole "finding" flow finished just yet, because of the smarter-search bits I mentioned earlier that haven't come up in a demo. When my library gets big, plain word-matching won't always be enough, and I'd expect:

- **Exact wording** — putting something in quotes so I get that phrase precisely, not every link that happens to contain those words scattered about.
- **Combining conditions** — being able to say something like "show me design links, but not the accessibility ones," or "this word *or* that word." Narrowing and excluding, not just one loose term.
- **Mixing a typed word with a label** in one go — e.g. links labeled "design" that also mention "grid."

Those matter to me for actually zeroing in when there's a lot saved. So I'd hold off on calling finding fully complete until I've seen that kind of more precise searching. The basics you've shown, though, are exactly right — I'm happy with those as the foundation.
